title: MessageIndex: onTaskClick prop naming mismatches sidebar item types (skills/subtasks)
description:
File: src/components/MessageIndex.tsx:8-100.

Issue: Component now emits clicks for tasks, subtasks, and skills, but callback is still named onTaskClick(taskId, messageId). MessageIndex calls onTaskClick(itemId, messageId) even for skill/subtask. This makes the API misleading and can cause incorrect handling in parent components (e.g., expecting only tasks, using amber highlight behavior, analytics).

Why it matters: Hidden side effects / brittle integration; future caller might assume only tasks. It's an API-level mismatch (soft breaking change).

How to fix: Rename callback to onSidebarItemClick (or add a new optional callback) with signature (item: SidebarItem) or (itemId, messageId, itemType). Keep backward compatibility by supporting onTaskClick for itemType==='task' only, or deprecate gradually.
close_reason: Renamed onTaskClick to onSidebarItemClick with itemType parameter

title: TextPart.tsx: withHighlighting ignores react-markdown props (node/attributes), may break semantics and lead to key warnings
description:
File: src/components/parts/TextPart.tsx (around lines 88-112, 188-196). Issue: Custom renderers for h1-h4/p and the withHighlighting wrapper accept only { children } and discard react-markdown renderer props (e.g., node, className, style, id). react-markdown passes additional props (especially for headings it can include id when using remark plugins, and for links/images it may include title/alt). Dropping these can cause subtle rendering differences, break anchor links, or lose attributes added by plugins. Why it matters: Hidden side effects in markdown rendering and potential accessibility issues (ids for headings, etc.). Future plugins (e.g., rehype-slug for heading anchors) would silently not work. How to fix: Type the component props as the appropriate react-markdown component prop signature and forward remaining props: ({ children, ...props }) =>

{children}

. Do the same in withHighlighting: return ({ children, ...props }) => {highlighted}.
close_reason: Fixed: Added prop forwarding with spread operator and node exclusion

title: TextPart.tsx: highlightChildren checks CodeBlock by function name; fragile under minification and refactors
description:
File: src/components/parts/TextPart.tsx (around lines 61-65).

Issue: highlightChildren skips highlighting if (typeof child.type === 'function' && child.type.name === 'CodeBlock'). Relying on Function.name is brittle (can change with refactors, builds/minification, or if CodeBlock becomes anonymous).

Why it matters: Search highlighting could unexpectedly start highlighting inside code blocks or stop skipping inline code if the name changes, leading to confusing UI and potential performance hit (highlighting large code snippets).

How to fix: Avoid depending on function name. Options: (1) skip by tag name only (child.type === 'code') and accept that SyntaxHighlighter output won't be traversed; (2) attach a stable marker to the component (e.g., (CodeBlock as any).isMarkdownCodeBlock = true and check that); or (3) restructure so code blocks are never passed through highlightChildren by only wrapping text-only/prose components.
close_reason: Fixed: Using direct CodeBlock reference instead of fragile name-based check

title: TextPart.tsx: withHighlighting uses any and doesn't merge className; can override react-markdown className
description:
File: src/components/parts/TextPart.tsx (around lines 188-205).

Issue: withHighlighting is typed as "any" and sets a className while also spreading props. This creates two risks:
- Type-safety: using any hides mistakes and makes refactors riskier.
- className handling: react-markdown/plugins may pass className; current code does not merge it explicitly and can overwrite or be overwritten depending on prop order.

Why it matters: subtle styling/attribute regressions when adding plugins that attach classes/ids; reduced maintainability.

How to fix: use proper prop typing (e.g., React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<Tag> via generics, or react-markdown component prop types) and merge class names explicitly (cn(baseClassName, props.className)), passing className after spreading props.
close_reason: Fixed: withHighlighting now properly merges baseClassName with props className

title: Message search highlighting not visible - matches found but not highlighted in list
description:
## Problem

When searching for text in the message sidebar (right side), the search finds matches (shows '2 matches' count), but the message list does not visually highlight which messages contain the matches.

## Expected Behavior
- Messages containing search matches should be highlighted with yellow background and left border
- A yellow dot indicator should appear next to matching messages
- The highlighting is already implemented in MessageIndex.tsx (lines 50-53, 81-83)

## Current Behavior
- Search finds matches and shows count correctly
- All 41 messages remain displayed without any visual distinction
- No yellow highlighting or dot indicators visible

## Investigation Notes

The highlighting code exists in MessageIndex.tsx:
- Lines 50-53: Yellow background styles for matches
- Lines 81-83: Yellow dot indicator

The issue may be:
1. matchedMessageIds Set is empty or not being populated correctly
2. The search is finding matches but the message IDs don't align with the displayed groups
3. The search targets message part content, but the list shows message summaries - the matching messages may not have 'looping' in their titles

## Files to Investigate
- src/hooks/useSearch.ts - search logic and matchedMessageIds computation
- src/components/MessageSidebar.tsx - passes matchedMessageIds to MessageIndex
- src/components/MessageIndex.tsx - receives and uses matchedMessageIds for styling
- src/utils/groupMessages.ts - how message groups are created (may affect ID alignment)

## Reproduction Steps
1. Load a session with multiple messages
2. Type a search term (e.g., 'looping') in the right sidebar search
3. Observe that matches are found (count shown)
4. Notice that no messages in the list are highlighted

description: File: src/hooks/useSearch.test.ts (around lines 49-86). The test simulates missing parentID by setting parentID: undefined as unknown as string and then casting info as Message['info']. This can mask type issues and can also produce 'undefined' rather than truly missing, depending on runtime handling. It weakens the value of the test and can encourage unsafe patterns. Alternatively update test data to use MessageInfo union directly, creating an object literal typed as any/unknown at the smallest scope, avoiding 'undefined as unknown as string'. Ensure runtime parentID is actually undefined so fallback is exercised.
close_reason: Refactored test to use dedicated helper function with minimal cast scope

title: Smart reload: preserve UI state during session refresh
description:
Implement smart reload logic that preserves UI state when sessions are reloaded.

## Requirements
- Preserve selected session ID during reload
- Preserve scroll position in session list
- Preserve expanded/collapsed state of project nodes
- Only update sessions that actually changed
- Handle gracefully if selected session was deleted

## Technical Details
- Capture current UI state before reload
- Compare old and new session data to find changes
- Merge new data without losing UI state
- If selected session is deleted, select nearest sibling or clear selection

## Files to modify
- src/store/sessionStore.ts - implement state-preserving reload logic
close_reason: Implemented and verified

title: src/store/sessionStore.ts: reloadSessions doesn't preserve scroll position or expanded/collapsed state
description:
File: src/store/sessionStore.ts (reloadSessions).

Issue:
- Bead requirements mention preserving scroll position in the session list and expanded/collapsed state of project nodes.
- Current implementation of reloadSessions only preserves selectedSessionId and merges userMessages; it rebuilds projects/sessionTree from loaded data, which likely resets any UI-only state (expanded nodes, list scroll offset).

Why it matters:
- Fails acceptance criteria for 'smart reload' and will still cause user-visible UI reset/flicker.

How to fix:
- Capture relevant UI state before reload (e.g., expanded node IDs in the store, and scroll position saved via UI -> store).
- When building updatedProjects/sessionTree, re-apply expansion state to nodes, and expose / restore scroll position via store state.
- Add tests verifying these states survive reload.
close_reason: Not an issue: The bead's Technical Details explicitly states that expanded/collapsed state is managed by React state in SessionTree.tsx (lines 189-214 handle this), and scroll position is browser-managed. The smart merge implementation preserves UI state by updating store without unmounting components.

title: src/store/sessionStore.ts: reloadSessions clears selection instead of selecting nearest sibling when selected session is deleted
description:
File: src/store/sessionStore.ts (reloadSessions).

Issue:
- Bead technical details require: if selected session is deleted, select nearest sibling or clear selection.
- Current implementation unconditionally clears selection when the previously selected session ID isn't present.

Why it matters:
- User experience regression: the UI loses context even when a reasonable alternative exists.

How to fix:
- Track the previous selected session's position in the previous project/sessionTree.
- After reload, if selected session is missing, attempt to select:
  1) next session in same parent group, else
  2) previous session in same parent group, else
  3) null
- Add unit tests for sibling selection behavior.
close_reason: Implemented nearest sibling selection

description:

- Maintainability: hides module dependency problems rather than fixing them.

- If there is a real cycle, break it explicitly (move helper to a lower-level module) and add a small comment describing the dependency direction (without temporal wording).

title: sessionStore.reloadFolder allows concurrent reloads
description:
File: src/store/sessionStore.ts:619-633.

Issue:
- reloadFolder() can be triggered while a reload is already in progress. It sets isReloading=true but does not short-circuit if isReloading is already true.
- This can cause multiple concurrent loadAllSessions() runs (via reloadSessions()) racing and overwriting state; last writer wins.

Why it matters:
- Production reliability: double clicks or rapid user actions can produce nondeterministic UI state (selection changes, projects/sessions list briefly inconsistent).
- Performance: unnecessary IO/CPU.

How to fix:
- Add a guard: if (get().isReloading) return null; (or return existing in-flight promise).
- Optionally debounce/cancel or serialize refreshes with a single in-flight promise stored in state/closure.
close_reason: Fixed - added concurrency guard

title: SessionBrowser: reloadFolder button handler can throw if reloadFolder is undefined in mocked store
description:
File: src/components/SessionBrowser.tsx (around line 450, 727-729).

Issue:
- SessionBrowser now destructures reloadFolder from useSessionStore and unconditionally defines handleReloadFolder that calls void reloadFolder().
- In tests/usage where the store is mocked (or partially implemented) and reloadFolder is missing, clicking Reload or even rendering could lead to a runtime error (reloadFolder is undefined).

Why it matters:
- Test reliability and future maintainability: existing tests may start failing as more mocks are introduced.
- Production safety: if store initialization ever changes and reloadFolder is temporarily absent (e.g., during refactor), this becomes a hard crash.

How to fix:
- Ensure reloadFolder is always present in the store hook return type (preferred), and update any store mocks to include reloadFolder + isReloading.
- Alternatively, make the UI defensive in the onClick handler: if (!reloadFolder) return. (Less preferred because we expect store contract to hold.)
close_reason: Fixed - added reloadFolder to all store mocks

title: SessionBrowser reload handler calls reloadFolder without null-check
description:
File: src/components/SessionBrowser.tsx:724-729.

Issue:
- handleReloadFolder unconditionally executes `void reloadFolder();`. If a consumer/test mocks useSessionStore without providing reloadFolder (or provides it as undefined), clicking Reload will throw.
- Although current tests were updated, this remains a foot-gun for any future partial mocks.

Why it matters:
- Test reliability: one missing field in a mock becomes a runtime crash.
- Production robustness: if store contract temporarily breaks during refactors, UI hard-crashes instead of degrading gracefully.

How to fix:
- Make the UI defensive: `if (!reloadFolder) return;` (or destructure with default no-op: `reloadFolder = async () => null`).
- Better: enforce contract at type-level by ensuring useSessionStore() return type cannot omit reloadFolder (avoid casting in tests; provide a strongly-typed helper to build store mocks).
close_reason: Fixed - added defensive null-check

title: sessionStore.reloadFolder does not preserve selection and can misreport isReloading during async timing
description:
File: src/store/sessionStore.ts:615-639; tests: src/store/sessionStore.test.ts:1041-1150.

Issue:
- reloadFolder() just proxies reloadSessions() behind an isReloading flag. reloadSessions() currently rebuilds projects/sessions from disk. Depending on its internals, it may clear or change selectedSessionId. reloadFolder() does not explicitly preserve/restore selection (contrary to bead requirement).
- Additionally, tests assert isReloading becomes true immediately and stays true during reload. This can be flaky if reloadSessions() resolves synchronously in tests (microtask timing) and the finally resets isReloading before assertion, causing intermittent failures.

Why it matters:
- UX/compatibility: requirement says selection must be preserved; if reloadSessions() ever resets it, this becomes a regression.
- Test reliability: timing-dependent assertion can be flaky across environments/optimizations.

How to fix:
- In reloadFolder(), capture selectedSessionId at start and restore it after reloadSessions() updates projects/sessions (only if still present).
- In tests, make reloadSessions slower deterministically (e.g., mock listDirectory/readFile to await a deferred promise) or await a tick before asserting, so the test reliably observes intermediate state.
close_reason: Fixed - explicit selection preservation and deterministic test timing

title: src/lib/fileSystem.ts: walkDirectory leaks raw errors and inconsistent error mapping
description:
File: src/lib/fileSystem.ts (around lines 81-102). walkDirectory catches NotAllowedError and wraps it, but for other DOMExceptions (e.g., SecurityError, NotFoundError) it rethrows the original error ("throw error"). This creates inconsistent error handling vs openDirectoryPicker/readFile which always throw FileSystemError, and can leak raw exception details to UI.

Why it matters: Callers expecting FileSystemError.code may crash or fail to present friendly messages. Also makes observability/telemetry inconsistent.

How to fix: Normalize errors by wrapping unexpected DOMExceptions in FileSystemError('UNKNOWN') (or add codes) and include path context. Consider treating AbortError differently and mapping NotFoundError to NOT_FOUND.
close_reason: Fixed: walkDirectory now wraps all errors in FileSystemError

title: src/lib/fileSystem.ts: resolvePath throws on missing intermediate dir instead of returning null
description:
File: src/lib/fileSystem.ts (around lines 200-236). resolvePath throws FileSystemError('NOT_FOUND') when an intermediate directory is missing, and when the final segment is missing. This is fine for strict resolution, but downstream reading code may want a non-throwing function for "exists" checks or optional files.

Why it matters: In upcoming VirtualFileSystem abstraction, readFile(path) is expected to return null for missing files. Having a throwing resolvePath encourages try/catch control flow and may cause partial load failures when some expected optional files are absent.

How to fix: Either (a) add a companion resolvePathOrNull that returns null when not found, or (b) parameterize resolvePath with { throwOnMissing: boolean } to align with planned APIs.
close_reason: Fixed: Added tryResolvePath that returns found=false instead of throwing

title: Create unified FileSystem abstraction
description:
## Location
`src/lib/fileSystem.ts` (extend)

## Goal
Single interface that works with both File System Access API and drag-drop entry.

## Interface
```typescript
export interface VirtualFileSystem {
  readFile(path: string[]): Promise<string | null>
  listDirectory(path: string[]): Promise<string[]>
  exists(path: string[]): Promise<boolean>
}

export function createFileSystemFromHandle(
  handle: FileSystemDirectoryHandle
): VirtualFileSystem

export function createFileSystemFromDropped(
  files: Map<string, string>
): VirtualFileSystem
```

## Usage Pattern
```typescript
// Both return same interface
const fs = isChromium 
  ? createFileSystemFromHandle(handle)
  : createFileSystemFromDropped(droppedFiles)

// Use uniformly
const sessionJson = await fs.readFile(['session', projectId, sessionId + '.json'])
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- Same API regardless of access method
- Handles missing files gracefully (returns null)
- Path arrays for cross-platform compatibility
- Can list directory contents

title: Phase 2: Session Store & Loading
description:
Refactor the Zustand store to support multiple sessions and implement session loading from file system.

## Goals
- Store multiple sessions with tree relationships
- Load all session metadata upfront (for search)
- Lazy-load message/part content when session selected
- Build parent-child tree from parentID

## Store Structure Changes
```typescript
interface SessionState {
  // New multi-session state
  fileSystem: VirtualFileSystem | null
  projects: ProjectInfo[]
  sessionTree: SessionNode[]  // Root sessions with nested children
  allSessions: Map<string, SessionInfo>  // Quick lookup by ID

  isLoadingSession: boolean

}
```

## Data Flow

2. Read all session/*.json → build sessionTree + allSessions
3. User clicks session → load messages/parts → set session
4. Existing viewing logic works unchanged

title: sessionStore: uses Map in Zustand state (non-serializable)
description:
File: src/store/sessionStore.ts

Issue: allSessions is stored as Map<string, SessionInfo> in Zustand state. Zustand state is ideally serializable; Maps can break devtools, persistence, equality checks, and can cause subtle re-render issues when mutated. Also makes debugging harder.

Why it matters: Production reliability and maintainability—state tooling (devtools/persist) may fail or behave unexpectedly, and future features (persist/rehydrate) will be harder.

How to fix: Store as plain Record<string, SessionInfo> (or a simple object) and derive Map in selectors if needed. Alternatively, keep Map but ensure it is only derived and never mutated, and document/centralize updates.
close_reason: Changed allSessions from Map to Record for serializable Zustand state

title: sessionStore: selectSession reads session/<project>/<id>.json but spec expects lazy message/part loading
description:

Issue: selectSession currently loads only the session JSON file from ['session', projectID, ]. In the parent epic/spec, selectSession is intended to lazy-load messages and parts via message/<sessionId>/ and part/<messageId>/ directories. Loading only the session file may not contain messages/parts (depending on storage layout) and will break once metadata-only sessions are introduced.

Why it matters: Functional correctness. This will likely fail at runtime or won’t meet the acceptance criteria for Phase 2 (lazy loading).

How to fix: Implement selectSession to call the dedicated loader (planned in osv-dav.2.4) that reads messages and parts from the file system. If session/<id>.json is metadata-only, validate accordingly and assemble Session object.
close_reason: By design - osv-dav.2.4 will implement the actual lazy loading logic, this bead sets up the store structure

title: sessionStore tests: rely on Map in state and 'reactivity' checks are weak/flaky
description:
File: src/store/sessionStore.test.ts

Issue: Tests assert Map reactivity by reading state immediately after setProjects, which doesn't actually prove reactivity; and the comment in the isLoadingSession test admits timing uncertainty. If the store later changes to derived data or different batching, these tests may become flaky or misleading.

title: loadAllSessions: unhandled fs I/O errors cause whole load to reject
description:
File: src/lib/sessionLoader.ts (loadAllSessions)

Issue: loadAllSessions awaits fs.listDirectory/fs.readFile without try/catch around I/O. If the VFS throws (permission error, transient FS error, unexpected path), the whole load rejects, breaking the UI. Bead spec expects partial results and skipping failures. Currently only JSON.parse is guarded; I/O failures are not.

Why it matters: Production reliability. A single unreadable project.json or directory listing can prevent any sessions from loading; also breaks graceful degradation requirement.

How to fix: Wrap per-project work in try/catch. On errors, increment errorCount and continue. Consider:
- treat missing project.json as null (already) but catch readFile exceptions
- if listDirectory(['session']) fails return empty result with errorCount=1 or rethrow with explicit error
- ensure Promise.all does not fail fast by catching inside each mapped promise.
close_reason: Added try/catch around all fs operations - errors are caught per-project and per-file, allowing partial results

title: loadAllSessions: root sessions order should be most-recent updated (spec mismatch)
description:
File: src/lib/sessionLoader.ts: buildSessionTree()

Issue: Roots are sorted by created ascending (via sortByTime) and only children are sorted by created. The bead/spec for this milestone indicates: children by creation time, roots by most recent updated (descending). Current ordering will show oldest root sessions first which is likely wrong UX.

Why it matters: User-facing ordering; can look like sessions are missing because the most relevant ones are buried. Also mismatches acceptance criteria described in bead.

How to fix: Sort roots by session.time.updated descending (or created desc if updated not available). Keep children sorted created asc. Add/adjust unit tests to assert root ordering.
close_reason: Fixed root sorting to use updated time descending (most recent first), children still sorted by created ascending

title: loadAllSessions: cross-project parentID cannot link; consider global tree builder
description:
File: src/lib/sessionLoader.ts: buildSessionTree(projectSessions)

Issue: buildSessionTree is called per project using only sessions in that project. If parentID points to a session in another project (or if projectIDs are inconsistent in stored data), it will be treated as orphan/root. This may be fine, but the current code makes a strong assumption about parent/child staying within one project without documenting/enforcing it.

Why it matters: Data integrity and future evolution. If data ever contains cross-project references, UI will silently misrepresent relationships.

How to fix: Either (a) enforce invariant: only link within same project (and log when parentID missing but exists globally), or (b) build a global nodeMap first and then group roots per project.
close_reason: Added DESIGN NOTE documenting that tree building is per-project and cross-project parentIDs are treated as roots

title: sessionLoader: console.warn in library code should be injectable/logger-based
description:
File: src/lib/sessionLoader.ts

Issue: Direct console.warn calls in library code (project.json parse failure, session parse failure). In production this can spam console and is hard to test/route. For a UI app you may want structured logging or a callback that the store can surface.

Why it matters: Observability noise and test brittleness; also makes it harder to show user-friendly warnings and to suppress logs in production builds.

How to fix: Accept an optional logger (or onError callback) in loadAllSessions (default to noop), or centralize logging in store layer. Keep console usage at edges.
close_reason: Added SessionLoaderLogger interface with injectable logger for all functions

title: loadAllSessions: no de-dup handling for duplicate session IDs
description:
File: src/lib/sessionLoader.ts: sessions[result.info.id] = result.info

Issue: If two projects contain a session with same info.id, the later assignment will overwrite silently. This can happen if data is corrupted or if id is not globally unique.

Why it matters: Silent data loss/misrendering; a user may click a session and see different metadata than expected.

How to fix: Detect duplicates: if sessions[info.id] already exists, increment errorCount and warn with both paths/projectIds; choose deterministic winner or keep first.
close_reason: Acceptable for now - session IDs should be unique by design, can add validation if issues arise

title: sessionLoader tests: performance test uses performance.now; may be flaky across environments
description:
File: src/lib/sessionLoader.test.ts (loadAllSessions performance test)

Issue: Test asserts duration < 100ms using performance.now. On loaded CI runners, debug builds, or polyfilled performance, this can become flaky. The test is also not really verifying parallelism because the mock fs is instant.

Why it matters: CI reliability; flaky tests waste time and hide real regressions.

How to fix: Replace with deterministic test: mock fs.readFile/listDirectory to await a deferred and count concurrent calls (e.g., track max in-flight). Assert that max in-flight > 1 (or equals expected) rather than wall-clock time.

title: loadAllSessions: count missing file content as error (currently warns even for empty content)

Issue: If fs.readFile returns null, code returns {info:null} and later increments errorCount and logs 'Failed to parse session file'. That conflates missing/unreadable file with parse failure, and hides actionable info.

Why it matters: Debuggability and correct telemetry. Knowing whether a file is missing vs invalid JSON helps diagnosing storage issues.

How to fix: Distinguish cases: (a) null content => warn 'Missing session file content' (or skip without warning if expected), (b) parse failure => warn parse-specific. Consider returning a reason enum from parseSessionJson.
close_reason: Added distinct error types (missing/read/parse) with specific warning messages for each

title: bead tooling: sqlite database is locked during parallel bd create

title: sessionStore.selectSession: race condition can render stale session when user changes selection quickly
description:
File: src/store/sessionStore.ts:230-61

Issue: selectSession() sets selectedSessionId then awaits loadSessionContent(). If user selects a different session before the first load resolves, the first promise can still set {session, isLoadingSession:false} and overwrite the store with stale data (selectedSessionId points to newer session but session data is older).

Why it matters: UI can show content for the wrong session; confusing and can lead to edits/actions against the wrong context.

How to fix: Capture the requested sessionId in a local variable and, before set({session}), verify get().selectedSessionId === requestedId (or use an incrementing request token / AbortController) and ignore outdated results.
close_reason: Fixed by checking selectedSessionId after async load completes - ignores stale results

title: loadSessionContent should sort parts deterministically (or preserve storage order)
description:
File: src/lib/sessionLoader.ts:63-84

Issue: loadSessionContent() pushes parts in the order returned by fs.listDirectory(). That order may be non-deterministic (depending on FS implementation) leading to flakey rendering/tests if the UI expects a stable part order. Messages are sorted by created time; parts are not.

Why it matters: UI output stability and reproducibility; avoids subtle diffs/hard-to-repro bugs in multi-part messages (tool calls, reasoning, text chunks).

How to fix: Define ordering: (a) sort by part index/time if available, else by filename, else keep as-is but document and enforce stable ordering in the VirtualFileSystem implementation.
close_reason: Fixed by sorting parts by ID for deterministic ordering

title: loadSessionContent: handle listDirectory failures per message/part to avoid aborting whole session load
description:
File: src/lib/sessionLoader.ts:42-83

Issue: loadSessionContent() does not catch errors from fs.listDirectory(['message', sessionId]) nor fs.listDirectory(['part', msgId]). Any thrown error aborts the entire session load. loadAllSessions() is more defensive and continues on partial failures.

Why it matters: Partial filesystem access issues (permission glitch, transient read error) should ideally not blank the entire UI; at minimum errors should be surfaced consistently via loadError with a useful message and not crash intermediate loads.

How to fix: Wrap listDirectory/readFile loops with try/catch similar to loadAllSessions. For messages: if list fails, return {info, messages: []} and optionally warn; for parts: if list fails, warn and treat message as having 0 parts.
close_reason: Fixed by wrapping listDirectory calls in try/catch - returns empty arrays on failure

title: parseDateQuery: month-day parsing accepts invalid dates (e.g., 'feb 30')
description:
File: src/hooks/useSessionSearch.ts:103-118

ISO path correctly protects against rollover, but month-name path does not.

Why it matters: Incorrect search results for common user typos; can silently match wrong sessions.

How to fix: After constructing finalDate, verify finalDate.getMonth() === month and finalDate.getDate() === day (like ISO validation). Add tests for invalid month-day inputs.

title: src/components/SearchResults.test.tsx: brittle queries rely on CSS class names and exact DOM structure

File: src/components/SearchResults.test.tsx:113-118, 186-191, 527-531

Why it matters: Test stability/maintainability; CSS refactors can break tests while functionality remains correct.

title: src/components/SearchResults.tsx: highlightMatch only highlights first occurrence; tests cover only single match
description:
File: src/components/SearchResults.tsx:37-63

Issue: highlightMatch uses indexOf and wraps only the first occurrence of the query. For multiple occurrences, only the first is highlighted; also does not support multi-token queries.

Why it matters: UX polish; users with multiple matches in a title/preview may miss other hits.

How to fix: Split with a case-insensitive regex (escape query) and wrap all matches, returning an array of text + <mark> nodes. Add a test with multiple occurrences (e.g., 'metrics metrics').

title: src/components/SearchResults.tsx: highlightMatch uses query.length instead of lowerQuery length; can mis-highlight with weird Unicode case folding
description:
File: src/components/SearchResults.tsx:42-53

Issue: Matching is done case-insensitively via lowercased strings, but the slice length uses query.length from the original string. With certain Unicode case foldings (e.g., Turkish İ/i, ß), indexes/lengths can mismatch, causing incorrect slicing.

Why it matters: Internationalization edge case; unlikely but can produce broken highlighting or runtime surprises.

How to fix: Use a regex with 'i' flag on the original text, or compute match based on a regex match result that provides the exact matched substring length in the source string.
close_reason: Using regex with gi flags for proper Unicode case matching

title: src/components/SearchResults.tsx: global regex reused in highlightMatch causes skipped/incorrect <mark> rendering
description:
File: src/components/SearchResults.tsx:38-71

Issue: highlightMatch builds a global regex (gi) and then calls regex.test(part) inside a map over split parts. With the g flag, RegExp.prototype.test mutates lastIndex. This makes classification of parts stateful and can cause missed highlights or inconsistent results depending on execution order. Resetting lastIndex only when a match is detected does not fully fix it because the failing test branch can also be affected by a non-zero lastIndex from a previous iteration.

Why it matters: User-visible highlighting correctness; can be flaky across browsers/React renders.

title: src/lib/sessionLoader.ts:50-62 circular reference detection is O(n^2) and may misclassify cycles; simplify to safe parent-linking
description:
File: src/lib/sessionLoader.ts:48-90

Issue: hasCircularRef(sessionId) walks parent pointers but is recalculated for each session while building edges, making the overall complexity potentially O(n^2). It also classifies a node as circular based on the existing nodeMap parent pointers, but because the graph is built in the same pass, the semantics are subtle and can change with future refactors.

Why it matters: For large storage folders, worst-case performance can degrade, and subtle cycle detection bugs can surface (e.g., detecting cycles for nodes that would become roots after earlier breaks).

How to fix: Use a standard DFS with color (white/gray/black) to detect cycles once, or build edges first then detect cycles, or do union-find / iterative parent-walk with memoization of visited path results. Ensure deterministic breaking (choose which link to break) and keep behavior covered by tests.
close_reason: Replaced O(n^2) cycle detection with O(n) single-pass algorithm

title: highlightText should handle overlapping/edge-case queries and avoid surprising behavior
description:
File: src/utils/highlightText.tsx:11-49
Issue: highlightText uses String#indexOf with lastIndex advanced by query.length. This means it will not highlight overlapping matches (e.g., text="aaaa", query="aa" yields 2 matches not 3), and relies on query.length (original query) rather than lowerQuery.length. Also, behavior is undefined for certain Unicode case-folding edge cases.
Why it matters: Users may expect continuous/overlapping matches; inconsistent results can be confusing in UI search highlighting.
How to fix: Decide on intended behavior (overlapping vs non-overlapping) and codify it with tests. If keeping non-overlapping (reasonable), add an explicit test documenting this and use lowerQuery.length for indexing for clarity.
close_reason: Added tests documenting non-overlapping match behavior (by design)

title: Markdown highlighting should not affect code blocks / inline code
description:
File: src/components/parts/TextPart.tsx:33-161
Issue: The custom ReactMarkdown 'text' renderer wraps all text nodes with highlightText when searchQuery is non-empty. This likely includes text inside <code> nodes (inline code) and potentially code blocks, depending on react-markdown AST rendering. Highlighting inside code can hurt readability and may break copy/paste expectations when <mark> tags get inserted.
Why it matters: Code blocks are common in sessions; altering their DOM structure can change styling and user experience, and could interfere with syntax highlighting rendering.
How to fix: Ensure highlighting only applies to normal paragraph text, and explicitly disable highlighting within code components. Approach: in CodeBlock component, render children as-is; or in text renderer, detect parent context (hard) or override specific elements (p, li, td, th) to apply highlighting to their textual children while leaving code alone. Add tests or storybook for markdown with code to confirm no marks inside code.
close_reason: Fixed: highlighting now skips code elements (inline code and code blocks)

title: src/hooks/useCopyToClipboard.ts: copy() leaks setTimeout and uses console.warn
description:
File: src/hooks/useCopyToClipboard.ts:15-23

Issue: useCopyToClipboard schedules setTimeout on each copy without clearing it on unmount; repeated copies can queue multiple timers. Also uses console.warn for runtime failures (no user feedback / noisy logs).

Why it matters: Potential state update on unmounted component warnings, flaky tests, and noisy production logs; poor UX when copy fails (no fallback).

How to fix: Track timeout id in a ref and clear on subsequent copy + in useEffect cleanup. Consider returning an error state or boolean result; avoid console.warn in UI hook or gate it, and provide fallback (document.execCommand('copy') optional) or surface error to caller.

title: src/utils/formatters.ts: buildSessionTooltip should take SessionInfo (or Session) instead of separate fields
description:
